frontier.hypothesis: Defeat jump2/find_cross_jump on the shared-v/shared-jal m2c-shape by making the TRUE and FALSE final `or` insns structurally distinct (different operand orders or intermediate register assignments) so cross-jump refuses to merge them — this preserves target's byte layout WHILE keeping the shared jal site.
frontier.mechanism: jump2 refuses to merge tails when they differ in any register operand. If FALSE arm can be structured so its final or emits as `or a0,v1,a0` (b LEFT in $v1) while TRUE arm's final or remains `or a0,a0,v0`, the tails differ and merge is blocked. The remaining wall is the same: getting b into $v1 requires target's [b,r,g] emission order. But in the shared-v shape, RA context differs (v is cross-arm-live) which MAY steer sched1 differently than the arm-local case. Unmeasured in s7 (s7 measured raw-halfword in arm-local baseline shape, not m2c-shape).
frontier.next_probe: Re-apply m2c-shape (shared v, shared gnd_load_tex(v)) but ALSO stage the raw halfword `b_stage = *(s16*)(p+2); if (b_stage >= 0)` in loop1 to force pseudo-78 fusion. Measure whether the combined shared-v + loop1-fusion form reaches score < 12 (or better, unlocks target byte layout). Two axes together may produce different sched1/jump2 interaction than either alone. NB: loop1 raw-halfword staging was s7-KILLED in ARM-LOCAL shape (2->11); the question is whether the shared-v shape has different RA that no longer displaces p.

frontier.hypothesis: The m2c reconstruction of the ORIGINAL source structure (shared v, shared jal) is the correct semantic shape but our fork's cross-jump is more aggressive than cc1psx's — an unmeasured axis is whether the shared-v with explicit intermediate arithmetic (splitting the OR into separate statements per arm) can produce enough arm-distinct RTL that jump2 doesn't merge past the final or.
frontier.mechanism: If FALSE arm is `v = *(u8*)(player+0x1A); v |= *(u8*)(player+0x18)<<16; v |= *(u8*)(player+0x19)<<8;` (three separate |= statements building v), the RTL has three SETs to v accumulating. TRUE arm builds v as `v = func_8004881C(...); v = (v<<16)|(v<<8)|v;`. Different structure per arm may leave jump2 with tails too dissimilar to merge past the final or.
frontier.next_probe: Apply shared-v + three-`|=`-statement FALSE arm form; sandbox --disable all; if score < 12, dump disasm to see whether jump2 kept arm-distinct final or's. Compare to raw m2c-shape (single-OR-expression) result.
